data.title: Neuronetics a new buy at B Riley on interventional psychiatry platform
data.description:
• B Riley has initiated Neuronetics (STIM) at buy, saying that the company is set to benefit from a psychedelic-driven shift in interventional psychiatry.
  • The investment bank has a $5 price target (~66% upside based on Sept. 10 close). 
  • While Neuronetics has traditionally focused on transcranial magnetic stimulation ("TMS") treatment for depression, its late-2024 acquisition of Greenbrook TMS "transformed Neuronetics from a transcranial magnetic stimulation capital equipment vendor into a vertically integrated interventional psychiatry platform."
  • Analyst Madison El-Saadi said that the deal added Greenbrook's 93-center clinic network that provides both TMS and treatment with Johnson & Johnson's (JNJ) Spravato (esketamine), a drug related to ketamine, which has hallucinogenic effects. Spravato's US sales surpassed a $2B run rate in Q1.
  • He noted that the company has replaced executives this year with a new CEO, CFO, and chief legal officer, adding that revenue is increasing and Q2 was its first adjusted EBITDA-positive quarter.
  • "STIM’s valuation understates Greenbrook’s growth profile, in our opinion, with the stock trading at a bottom-quartile multiple despite its services segment growing above peer averages," El-Saadi wrote.

data.title: US regulators look to create framework for risks associated with banks' third-party ties
data.description:
U.S. regulators are looking to create a framework to assist financial institutions with managing risks associated with third-party relationships.

In a joint statement, the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, the Federal Reserve Board, the National Credit Union Administration, and the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency requested public comments on its proposed guidance.

"Banking organizations routinely rely on third parties for a range of products, services, and other activities," said the joint statement. "The agencies have long acknowledged both the benefits associated with third-party relationships and the potential that these relationships may present or, in some cases, heighten certain risks."

"The proposed guidance would address these concerns by emphasizing risk identification and assessment as the foundation of a risk-based approach. This would enable banking organizations and examiners to focus on material financial risks and violations of laws and regulations rather than ineffective and counterproductive check-the-box exercises," said the statement.

"The proposed guidance would also encourage responsible innovation, consistent with Executive Order 14405, by emphasizing a risk-based and tailored approach to third-party risk management and removing broad-based and overly prescriptive language from the 2023 Guidance that may unduly impede fintechs from entering partnerships with banking organizations," said the guidance.

The comments are due 60 days after publication in the Federal Register.

The non-binding principles-based approach intends to assist banks and credit unions to better align and tailor their third-party risk management practices to the risks of individual third-party relationships.

data.title: SPS Commerce jumps on report GTCR in talks to purchase
data.description:
SPS Commerce (SPSC) rose 11% after a report that private equity firm GTCR is in discussions to buy the supply chain software maker. 

A deal could be announced in the coming weeks, according to a Bloomberg report on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter. No transaction has been finalized, and talks could still fall apart, or another buyer could emerge.

GTCR declined to comment to Bloomberg.  SPS Commerce declined to comment.

The news comes after Reuters reported in June that SPS Commerce (SPSC) was considering a sale and had engaged Morgan Stanley as an advisor.

Activist investors Irenic Capital Management and Anson Funds Management both obtained stakes  in the company and began advocating for a sale earlier this year.

Shares of Descartes Systems (DSGX), a peer of SPS (SPSC), advanced 7.4% on Friday.

data.title: To hike or not to hike: Economists duke it out over CPI
data.description:
The August Consumer Price Index report triggered debate among prominent economists over whether the Federal Reserve should raise interest rates at its upcoming meeting, exposing sharp disagreements over underlying inflation trends versus statistical noise.

Meanwhile, market-implied odds of a rate increase at next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting jumped sharply after the inflation data, with fed funds futures traders now pricing in a roughly 90% chance of a hike.

The case for a rate hike

RSM Chief Economist Joseph Brusuelas argued forcefully that the combined August Producer Price and Consumer Price Indices demand action from the Fed. He pointed to three persistent supply shocks—war-induced energy disruptions, tariffs driving up prices, and the draw on commodities and finished goods to support artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout—as forces that can no longer be dismissed as transitory.

"Seven months into what was thought to be a short-term conflict has simply turned into something else which now requires a rational policy response from the Federal Reserve," Brusuelas wrote in a social media post, noting that rising distillate prices for gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel are no longer being absorbed through firm margin compression but are instead showing up in groceries and services throughout the economy.

Brusuelas contended the Fed needs to remove the three rate cuts implemented in late 2025 to slow an economy growing well above trend, with nominal gross domestic product exceeding 6% in the second quarter, a deficit-to-GDP ratio above 6%, near-full employment, and record corporate profits. By forcing price increases back onto corporate balance sheets through margin compression, the central bank could provide relief to consumers facing an affordability crisis.

Oliver Allen of Pantheon Macroeconomics offered a more measured but still concerning assessment, noting that the breadth of CPI inflation captures the Fed's dilemma. While the share of CPI components annualizing above 3% remains below recent highs, it has stalled well above pre-pandemic averages.

"Chair Warsh is unlikely to be reassured," Allen said.

 

 

The case for patience

Not all economists see the August data as justification for tightening. Parker Ross urged caution in interpreting the 0.51% month-over-month jump in supercore CPI that briefly sent September rate hike odds surging to nearly 100%.

"Unless the Fed plans to hike rates to get your cell phone bill under control, I'd be careful reading too much into the spike," Ross wrote, revealing that wireless phone services alone contributed 29 basis points—more than half of the supercore increase. Combined with lodging away from home, these two notoriously volatile categories accounted for 14 of the 29 basis points in core CPI's rise.

Ross acknowledged the headline 0.40% monthly increase looked hot but noted energy contributed nearly 40% of that gain, while food added just 2 basis points. Looking at longer trends, he emphasized that August core CPI of 0.29% compares to a three-month average of roughly 0.16% and a six-month average of approximately 0.21%. "One noisy print doesn't make a new inflation trend," he concluded.

Marko Bjegovic took the sharpest stance against tightening, calling a potential rate hike "a huge policy error." He noted that core CPI stands at its lowest level since March 2021, meaning the Fed would be raising rates with core inflation at 5.5-year lows. "Core PCE is higher due to temporary statistical quirks that are concentrated in just a few components," Bjegovic argued. "That's not a reason to hike rates."

Looking ahead

The contrasting interpretations leave the Fed weighing whether to act against what some see as sticky, broad-based price pressures or to look through what others characterize as volatile, category-specific monthly noise. Brusuelas called the decision "truly a coin flip at this juncture," even as markets increasingly view a rate increase as the base case.

data.title: Rent the Runway outlines Q3 revenue of $87M-$90M backed by $15M rights offering and CEO transition
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Rent the Runway (RENT) Q2 2026

Management View

  • "This morning, we announced that Paige Thomas has been appointed as Rent the Runway's Chief Executive Officer, President and a Member of our Board of Directors effective September 14." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Teri Bariquit)

  • "Our strategy is supported by 3 operating objectives: total customer growth, profit expansion and operational excellence." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit)

  • "We are concentrating our resources toward improving our execution on rental and selling." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit) "First, we paused marketplace" and "We paused on-site advertising and monetization" and "We are not pursuing new B2B dry cleaning partners, though we will continue to serve the ones we have." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit)

  • "For the second quarter, we delivered $98 million in revenue, ahead of the range we communicated in June." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit)

  • "Engagement with this feature on our app is running at 35%, ahead of our expectations." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit) "During the pilot, customers with the outfit experience added to their bags 12% more often than those without it" and "77% of the time she opened another item within the look." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit)

  • "Today, we announced our plan to launch a rights offering to holders of our Class A common stock, backstopped by these investors, for $15 million to support the company's operational plans and liquidity." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit)

  • "We delivered $98 million in net revenue, an all-time record for the company." (Interim Chief Financial Officer David Loretta)

Outlook

  • "We are reiterating our double-digit revenue growth guidance for the full fiscal year 2026 and reiterating our adjusted EBITDA guidance of 4% to 7% of revenue for fiscal year 2026." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "For Q3 2026, we expect revenue to be between $87 million and $90 million, representing between flat to 3% growth versus Q3 2025." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "We expect Q3 adjusted EBITDA to be between negative 3% and negative 6% of revenue." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "We now expect rental product investment to be in the range of $53 million to $55 million in fiscal year '26" and "the change in this investment amount reflects our plans to remain flexible and dynamic with where we acquire rental inventory and also to ensure key fall events and new product launches in the second half are more fully stocked." (Interim CFO Loretta)

Financial Results

  • "Total revenue for the quarter was $97.7 million, up 20.8% year-over-year and up 8.7% quarter-over-quarter." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "Gross profit margin was 36.1% in Q2, versus 30% last year, representing a 609 basis point improvement." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "Adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter was $12.6 million or 12.9% of revenue, versus $3.6 million or 4.4% of revenue in Q2 of last year." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "We ended the second quarter with 140,826 active subscribers, down 3.8% year-over-year." (Interim CFO Loretta) "The decrease in ending active subscribers was driven primarily by a year-over-year increase in the rate of pause and the year-over-year decrease in the number of subscribers acquired due to the stronger use of promotions in 2025, which we have reduced this year." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "Free cash flow for year-to-date 2026 was negative $21.6 million, versus negative $32.9 million in year-to-date 2025." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • "Our liquidity position has strengthened with a $10 million term loan" and "we plan to launch an equity raise in the amount of $15 million to further bolster our liquidity position and support ongoing growth." (Interim CFO Loretta)

Q&A

  • No analyst Q&A session was included in this transcript.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts sentiment could not be assessed because "No analyst Q&A session was included in this transcript." (Operator)

  • Management tone in prepared remarks was slightly positive and execution-focused, including "we could not be more confident in our strategy" (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit) alongside "we are concentrating our resources" and "we have paused select pilots" to prioritize rental and selling execution. (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit)

  • Compared with the prior quarter, the current call emphasized leadership and liquidity actions, while the previous quarter’s prepared tone highlighted momentum and customer-led growth, including "our transformation strategy is working" and "We've seen a return to subscriber growth in Q1." (Co-Founder, CEO, President & Chairman Jennifer Y. Hyman)

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The current quarter introduced a CEO change and a financing plan, including "Paige Thomas has been appointed" and "plan to launch a rights offering...for $15 million" plus "a $10 million term loan." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit; Interim CFO Loretta)

  • The prior quarter positioned strategy around aggressive inventory build and product launches, including "we are planning our largest ever investment in new inventory this year" and "Q1 inventory volume received was up 24% year-over-year." (Co-Founder, CEO, President & Chairman Hyman)

  • The current quarter highlighted tighter sequencing and operational focus, including "we are concentrating our resources" and "we have paused marketplace" and "paused on-site advertising and monetization," while the prior quarter highlighted expansion initiatives such as "we're planning to launch a new rewards program" and broader growth pods. (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit; Co-Founder, CEO, President & Chairman Hyman)

Risks and Concerns

  • Subscriber pressure and seasonality were framed as a near-term headwind, with "the year-over-year growth in ending active subscriber count decelerated in Q2" and Q3 expected to be impacted by "the normal seasonality of higher subscription pause activations in Q3." (Interim CFO Loretta)

  • Execution focus was described as a mitigation, including "by concentrating our resources, we expect to improve execution and results." (Interim CEO, Interim President & Director Bariquit)

  • Liquidity actions were positioned as support for operating plans, including "a $10 million term loan" and the "backstopped rights offering...in the amount of $15 million to further bolster our liquidity position." (Interim CFO Loretta)

Final Takeaway

Management emphasized a leadership transition to Paige Thomas effective September 14, paired with sharper prioritization around the core rental and selling experience, including pausing marketplace and on-site advertising/monetization initiatives. The company reported record quarterly net revenue and expanded margins, while also flagging decelerating year-over-year ending active subscriber growth and expected Q3 seasonality from pauses. For liquidity and operating flexibility, management detailed a $10 million term loan and a planned $15 million backstopped rights offering, while reaffirming full-year 2026 guidance for double-digit revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA of 4% to 7% of revenue, and outlining Q3 revenue of $87 million to $90 million and adjusted EBITDA of negative 3% to negative 6% of revenue.

data.title: Spotify expands video partnership with music platform Genius
data.description:
Spotify (SPOT) on Friday said it is expanding its video offering through a partnership with music-lyrics platform Genius, adding episodes of two of Genius’ established artist-focused series to its service.

The agreement gives Spotify (SPOT) users access to full episodes of Open Mic, which features artists performing their songs in stripped-down settings. The platform will also carry older episodes of Verified, a series centered on artists explaining their lyrics and creative process, alongside new releases.

The move brings more music-related video content into Spotify (SPOT) as the company broadens the ways users interact with songs and artists. Genius said Open Mic and Verified have accumulated more than 3.7 billion views combined since their respective launches in 2016.

Rapsody is featured in the first new Open Mic episode under the expanded arrangement, performing “Pick A Side,” a track from her latest album, God Gotta Afro & Gold Hoops. New episodes are scheduled for Thursdays.

Verified will release new episodes twice a week, on Wednesdays and Fridays. This week’s episodes include Magnus Ferrell discussing “Asleep Talking” and JISOO examining “Click.”

The partnership builds on Spotify’s (SPOT) earlier rollout of Verified and gives Genius a wider distribution channel for its video programming.

Shares were trading around 2% higher on Friday.

data.title: Ørsted says it won favorable ruling from E.U. advisory commission in U.K. tax case
data.description:
Ørsted (DNNGY) said late Thursday that an advisory commission established under the European Union's Arbitration Convention issued a final opinion in the case between Denmark and the U.K. regarding taxation rights related to the Walney Extension and Hornsea 1 offshore wind farms.

The commission ruled Ørsted's (DNNGY) two British wind farms should be ​taxed primarily in Britain, supporting the company's position in a ‌dispute between Danish and U.K. tax authorities.

The case began in 2015, when Ørsted (DNNGY) approached the two tax authorities to avoid double taxation of the ​projects; after the authorities did not reach an agreement, they ​referred the matter to the advisory commission.

Danish authorities claimed 6.6B Danish ​crowns (~$1B) in taxes and interest related to the projects, which Ørsted (DNNGY) challenged, saying British subsidiaries developed, owned, and operated the projects and had already paid U.K. tax.

The commission found the projects had a "genuine legal and economic purpose" and were "primarily taxable" in the country where ​they are located ​and generate revenue, the company said.

Ørsted (DNNGY) said Friday that the ruling would entail a "minor upwards adjustment" to ​its tax position in Denmark, and "the tax ​charge in ⁠Denmark will, over time, largely be offset by tax reductions in the U.K."

data.title: Feds announce end to Cyclospora outbreak
data.description:
• The CDC on Friday declared that the Cyclospora outbreak that began in July and has sickened over 12,800 individuals has ended.
  • The agency noted that recent infections linked to the outbreak have dropped significantly. However, its investigation into the cause will continue. 
  • Citing two officials, The Washington Post first reported on Thursday that the end of the outbreak announcement was imminent.
  • The US identified Taylor Farms iceberg lettuce grown in Mexico as the source of the outbreak. That lettuce was served at Yum! Brands' (YUM) Taco Bell restaurants.
  • In mid-July, Taylor issued a recall. 
  • Michigan was hit the hardest by the outbreak. Two people in the state with underlying health conditions died after infection.

data.title: Dell, HPE and HP surge on AI enterprise demand and PC, server refresh
data.description:
Dell (DELL), Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and HP (HPQ) were all surging 8% or more during Friday morning market action due in part to a combination of sustained enterprise AI demand and a PC refresh.

HPE was also boosted due to strong earnings results from Oracle (ORCL). Earlier this month, the two companies announced a new partnership. Under the terms of the deal, Oracle plans to scale its AI global infrastructure by deploying HPE's routing and switching platforms across all its data centers. This is good news for HPE as Oracle's remaining performance obligations grew $209B during the first quarter to $664B, including more than $30B in additional AI cloud contracts. 

Meanwhile, Dell received an Outperform rating and $640 price target as RBC Capital Markets initiated coverage of the stock.

"DELL exited 2Q27 with $95bn in AI server backlog and a pipeline that continues to grow despite converting ~$132bn into orders over the LTM," said RBC analyst David Paige in an investor note. "We view the environment as supply-constrained (primarily memory) rather than demand-limited and expect a meaningful backlog to persist through FY27, providing visibility into FY28."

"Agentic AI is creating incremental CPU/traditional server demand to run orchestration layers, expanding the TAM for traditional compute," Paige added. "Additional vectors include enterprise server refresh (majority of installed base on 14G or older), PC refresh, data center consolidation, and AI inference migration. Large enterprises are entering multi-year arrangements (3-5 years) focused on securing supply access, suggesting visibility extends beyond near-term dynamics."

Meanwhile, RBC also initiated coverage on HP with a Sector Perform rating and a $33 target.

"We believe HPQ is well positioned to benefit from the confluence of AI PC adoption, the shift toward edge computing and enterprise requirements for data privacy, creating a multi-year tailwind for the PS segment," Paige noted. "HPQ is targeting AI PC shipments of 60-70% by FY27 (up from ~45% in 3Q26) as enterprises increasingly deploy local inference to address cloud token economics, latency constraints, and data governance requirements."
